items.name: text
items.title: Text
items.description: Paragraph text and the wrappers that pick the element for you: H1-H4, Span, and Label. Size, tone, weight and align are props; tone names a role (default, quiet, primary, danger, on-primary, on-danger) rather than a colour, so it follows the palette and mode. Heading level and size are independent, so the semantically correct level never forces a look. No loading state - place a Skeleton yourself, at the height the real text will take.

items.name: stack
items.title: Stack
items.description: VStack stacks children downward and HStack lays them out sideways, both with an 8px gap you never have to ask for. Gap takes Tailwind's own spacing scale rather than a second scale; align and justify are ordinary props, and HStack centres across the row because a row is nearly always something small beside a line of text. No loading state and no empty state - a stack takes arbitrary children, so it cannot tell empty from one child that renders nothing; place a Skeleton yourself.
